target_customer: Military small units (infantry and similar) needing counter-drone defence; also trainees of its Drone Warfare Academy
problem: Cheap hostile drones threaten small units that lack affordable ways to spot, engage and destroy them. Earendil sells sensors, autonomous interceptors and training covering the kill chain.
business_model: Defence hardware sales plus paid training academy
product_category: Counter-UAS hardware (interceptor drones, thermal sights, networked awareness)

founders.name: James Walton
previous_startups: Two IT and telecoms companies (unnamed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says UAS work in Ukraine.

founders.name: Dan Komorny
previous_startups: Multiple unnamed startups per YC launch text
founders.background_notes: About a decade in drones and security; built AR heads-up display applications, optical systems and drone payload hardware.

competitors.name: Ukrainian interceptor drone makers (Sting, Bullet, SkyFall P1-SUN, F-Drones)
competitors.what: Low-cost interceptor drones against Shahed-class drones
competitors.traction_then: More than 20 Ukrainian producers reported in early 2026; Pentagon in talks to buy

competitors.name: Tytan Technologies
competitors.what: Munich-based interceptor counter-drone system chosen by the Bundeswehr

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous interceptors, thermal optics and networked awareness are hardware plus autonomy problems for a seven person team.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals in the space. Combat-use claims and defence procurement relationships could help but are unverified.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say; first YC batch, with large defence players and funded startups in the same wedge.

market_need_then: Reports in 2026 describe heavy demand for cheap interceptors in Ukraine and Western interest in buying them.

identity.logo: White logo file exists; design not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Defence-technology look, product names Aeglos, AURION, Holo
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, urgent, confident short taglines such as Nobody fights blind

branding.brand_signature: Product family names and the Drone Warfare Academy

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct tone on its site but no independent press on the brand found. The name resembles Tolkien's Earendil and a 2026 Hacker News thread debates the name of an unrelated Earendil tech company.

outcome_analysis: Earendil Robotics is an Active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its founders have military and drone backgrounds and the company claims systems fielded in Ukraine. The wedge sits in a crowded and well funded counter-drone market, so proof of procurement will matter most.
notes: Unverified aggregator figures: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round and Nordic9 lists $500k of investments, with no dates or investors visible, so no round was recorded. Aggregators disagree on location (San Francisco vs London). Claims of combat use and intercepts come from the company's own pages. Founder education not found. Name origin not stated by the company. Completeness pass: the 125K seed (no date or investors shown) is recorded from Dealroom alone; Nordic9 lists 500K of investments and Caplight lists a YC accelerator entry on 2026-07-01.
